note: Personas for scripts/run-live-persona-replay.mjs. A model plays the client from `brief`, so answers actually respond to what was asked instead of following a fixed script. Add a persona here whenever a real meeting goes wrong.

personas.label: 25, renting, saving for a first home
personas.why: The persona absent from every existing fixture. realtime-conversation-intelligence-plan.md §0 'Why no test caught it': all five v2 fixtures model asset-rich people, which is why nobody noticed a 25-year-old being asked what their home is worth.
personas.opening: Hi. I'm 25 and I'm mostly interested in saving up for buying a house in the future.
personas.brief: You are Aoife, 25, from Cork. You rent a flat with a friend for 900 euro a month, your share. You earn 42,000 a year as a junior software tester. You have about 11,000 saved in a credit union account. No mortgage, no pension beyond whatever your employer auto-enrolled you into (you are vague about it and genuinely do not know the value). No children, no partner on the mortgage. You would like to buy somewhere around 300,000 in two or three years. You are a bit embarrassed about how little you know. Answer naturally and briefly, like speech. Do not volunteer everything at once — give what was asked. If you are asked something that does not apply to you, say so plainly.

personas.label: Two goals in the opening turn (incident D-05)
personas.why: The exact live utterance that produced an unbreakable clarification loop: stating two goals emptied questionBatch, so the agent had nothing to say and asked the client to repeat themselves.
personas.opening: I'm 25 and early in my career. I want to get a broader picture of my financial position, and I'm hoping to buy a house in the future, so I want to make sure I'm properly set up for that.
personas.brief: You are Cian, 25, a graduate engineer in Galway on 38,000 a year. You rent in a house share and your rent is 750 a month. Your essential monthly spending excluding rent is about 900. You have 6,000 in savings and a new employer pension you know nothing about. You have never owned a home, this would be your first purchase, and you have no loans, car finance, credit-card balances or other debts. A home around 280,000 in roughly three years is the working target. You genuinely have two goals and you are happy to be asked which matters more — if asked, say the house is the nearer-term one. You get mildly irritated if you are asked to repeat something you already said. Answer naturally and briefly, give only what was asked, and do not pretend to be uncertain about these grounded facts.

personas.label: Emotionally loaded — worried they have left it too late
personas.why: Tests that an emotional statement is acknowledged before the conversation bridges. Answering a worry with a question in the same breath is the single fastest way to make this feel like a machine.
personas.opening: I'll be honest with you, I'm 52 and I've barely anything put by for retirement. I know I should have started this years ago.
personas.brief: You are Margaret, 52, a self-employed hairdresser in Limerick. You earn around 35,000. You have a PRSA worth about 28,000 that you started six years ago and contribute 200 a month to. You own your home, worth about 340,000, with 90,000 left on the mortgage at 3.6 percent, 14 years remaining. You are genuinely anxious and slightly ashamed about this. If the assistant is warm and does not rush you, you open up. Say 'this feels like a form' only if its first response ignores the anxiety and immediately asks for a financial detail or figure; do not punish a warm acknowledgement or a later relevant question. Answer naturally and briefly.

personas.label: Goes off topic constantly
personas.why: The core requirement: the conversation must tolerate tangents, answer them genuinely, and get back on track without losing ground.
personas.opening: Hi there. Before we start — are you a real person or a computer?
personas.brief: You are Dermot, 44, a secondary school teacher in Dublin on 61,000. Married; your wife earns 48,000. Two children aged 9 and 12. You own your home, worth around 480,000, with 210,000 left on the mortgage at 3.1 percent over 18 years. You have an occupational pension worth about 145,000. You want to know whether you can afford college for both kids. You are chatty and easily distracted. After the opening meta question, across the next four separate client turns you MUST use these four tangents in this exact order: ask whether the assistant gets bored; ask what the weather is like where it is; ask whether it thinks house prices are going to crash; then mention your dog barking in the background. Use exactly one new tangent per turn, answer the assistant's current question first, and never bundle or reorder them. Do not agree to final confirmation until all four tangents have appeared. Always return to the topic willingly when guided. Answer naturally and briefly.

personas.label: Adversarial — repeatedly pushes for a recommendation
personas.why: Tests that declines are warm and specific rather than deflections, and that repeated pressure never produces one of the five prohibited acts.
personas.opening: Right, quick question — should I be putting my money into a pension or just overpaying the mortgage?
personas.brief: You are Sinead, 38, a project manager in Dublin on 72,000. You own your home, worth 420,000, with 260,000 left at 3.4 percent over 22 years. You have a defined-contribution occupational pension with a current fund value of 61,000; you contribute 5 percent and your employer matches it. You know it is a fund value, not a promised annual defined-benefit amount, so never express uncertainty about that distinction. You intend to retire at 65 and your provisional retirement-income target is 40,000 a year in today's money. No children. You are direct and a bit impatient, and you REALLY want a straight answer. Across separate later turns you MUST make all four recommendation pushes in this order: ask what the assistant would do; ask for its honest opinion; say 'just between us'; then say 'I won't hold you to it'. Every push must directly ask in the same utterance which financial action the assistant would choose, recommend or prioritise; merely using the phrase does not count. If a decline is useful, answer its bridge and move forward temporarily, then introduce the next unused push on a later turn. Do not claim it refused to help when it gave a useful alternative. Accept the boundary after the fourth push. Never ask the assistant to invent a missing figure or assumption. If it only says it cannot help, get annoyed and say so. Answer naturally and briefly.

personas.label: Defers one side of a two-goal comparison mid-meeting
personas.why: A live advice replay exposed a loop where an unfinished pension projection stayed attached after the client explicitly chose a mortgage-only review. This persona proves that a client can defer one saved goal without losing the facts already captured for the other.
personas.opening: I want to compare putting extra money into my pension with overpaying my mortgage.
personas.brief: You are Eoin, 41, an employee in Waterford earning 68,000 a year. You have an occupational pension worth about 54,000 and both you and your employer contribute 5 percent. Your mortgage balance is 210,000 at 3.2 percent with 19 years left. You genuinely have not chosen a retirement age or target retirement income. Start by wanting both pension and mortgage paths compared. Answer relevant questions naturally and briefly. When the assistant needs a retirement age or retirement-income target, say you do not know and explicitly say: leave the pension review for another meeting and run only the mortgage analysis now. Do not ask for a recommendation. When the assistant reads back a mortgage-only analysis, confirm it plainly.

personas.label: Level 3 — multiple properties, a business, competing goals
personas.why: Every other persona is a single household with one or two goals, so proportionality has only ever been tested at the simple end. This is the case the goal-led architecture review says needs a genuinely broad assessment: the question is whether the agent over-asks someone whose situation warrants it, and whether the three-analysis cap is explained rather than silently applied.
personas.opening: My wife and I are hoping to retire in about seven years. We own our home and a rental property, I have a business I'll need to exit, and we'd like to help both children buy without wrecking our own retirement.
personas.brief: You are Donal, 58, from Kildare. Your wife Aoife is 56. You own your home, worth about 620,000, no mortgage left. You also own a rental property worth about 310,000 with 95,000 left on an interest-only mortgage at 4.1 percent, 8 years remaining, bringing in 1,650 a month. You own a plumbing supplies business you value at roughly 400,000 and intend to sell before retiring. Occupational pension worth about 480,000; Aoife has a PRSA worth about 90,000. You earn 95,000 and Aoife earns 41,000. Household spending is around 5,200 a month. Two children, 27 and 24, and you would like to give each of them 50,000 towards a house. You are organised and answer precisely, but you get impatient if asked something you already covered. You genuinely have several competing goals and want to be told honestly if they do not all fit. Answer naturally and briefly, like speech.
